title: Chrome for accountants on Mac: setup, tips and Lazur for cloud ledger work
metaTitle: Chrome for Accountants on Mac: Setup, Tips and Lazur
description: Chrome for accountants on Mac: set up profiles, use tab groups and split view, save PDFs, and ask Lazur by voice while you work in cloud ledgers.
secondaryKeywords: Chrome tips for bookkeeping on Mac
Save as PDF in Chrome on Mac
Xero and QuickBooks Online in Chrome
intro: Chrome for accountants on Mac means using Google Chrome as the window for your cloud ledgers, bank feeds and client files. The setup that helps most is small: separate profiles, tab groups, split view, a careful print routine and only the extensions you trust. Lazur fits on top of that. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask a question, and it answers out loud while it sees your screen.
tldr: Use one Chrome profile per client group, so logins, cookies and autofill stay apart.
Tab groups and split view keep the ledger, bank feed and receipts inbox in view together.
Check the print preview before you save a PDF. Google's help page confirms ⌘P and File > Print.
Dextension adds Dext to Xero and QuickBooks Online. It works only in Chrome or Microsoft Edge, and you need a Dext account.
Lazur answers out loud, points at things and guides you one click at a time. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: Why Chrome matters for accounting work on a Mac

A lot of accounting work now happens in a browser tab. Xero and QuickBooks Online run in Chrome. So do supplier portals, bank feeds and the shared folders where clients send receipts. Chrome is the room you work in, so it pays to set it up once.

Google's own Chrome page lists the features that matter here. They are tab groups, vertical tabs, split view, Google Password Manager, Autofill, sync for bookmarks and saved passwords, and extensions from the Chrome Web Store. None of these are accounting features. They are the plumbing that keeps several client files open without chaos.

This guide covers those features in the order you need them. It also covers the parts Google does not explain well, such as printing a clean PDF. Lazur comes in near the end. The browser setup works without it.
Check your Chrome version before you change anything

Open Chrome > About Google Chrome on your Mac. The page shows your build number and whether an update is waiting. Sources disagree on the current version right now. WhatIsMyBrowser lists Chrome on macOS as 156.0.8078.82, released 2026-11-04. Google's Chrome Enterprise and Education release notes list Chrome 152, dated September 1, 2026. Trust the number on your screen, and update if the page asks you to.

The version matters because a stale build can misbehave on the sites you use every day. If a ledger page looks broken, check the version before you blame the page. Then retest the same page in the same profile.
Set up separate Chrome profiles for each client group

A Chrome profile keeps its own bookmarks, passwords, cookies and extensions. Click your profile picture in the top right of the Chrome window to switch or add one. Use a work profile for your firm and a separate one for personal browsing. If some clients must not see each other's data, give them separate profiles too.

The common mistake is one profile for everything. A Xero login for one client then sits beside a supplier portal for another. Autofill fills the wrong details on the wrong page. Tabs from the last client stay open during the next call.
Set up the work profile this way:

items: Click your profile picture, choose Add, and create a profile named for your firm.
Sign in with the work account in that profile only.
Turn on sync in that profile, so bookmarks and passwords follow you to your other Mac.
Install extensions in that profile, and remove any you do not use.
Keep client groups in separate profiles if their data must stay apart.

blocks.text: Passwords, Autofill and sync on a shared Mac

Google Password Manager stores logins for each profile. You find its settings under Chrome > Settings, in the Autofill and passwords section. Review the saved logins before you share the Mac, and delete entries for clients you no longer serve. Autofill also keeps addresses and other details, so review those too.

Sync copies bookmarks and saved passwords across devices. That helps when you move between a desk Mac and a laptop. It also means a login follows you to every device where the profile is signed in. Turn sync off on a machine you lend out, or sign out of the profile first.

blocks.title: Before you lend the Mac
blocks.text: Sign out of the work profile, then clear browsing data. Press ⌘⇧⌫ to open the clear data window, or go through Chrome > Settings. [Our guide](/how-to/clear-browsing-data-in-chrome) walks through the options, step by step.
Tab groups and split view for ledger and bank work

A typical close involves the ledger, the bank feed and an inbox of receipts. Keeping those in one window is the first win. Right-click a tab and choose Add tab to new group. Name the group after the client and pick a color. Collapse the group when you need the screen back.

Split view puts two tabs side by side. Use it to match bank lines to invoices, or to compare a supplier statement with the ledger balance. Google's Chrome page confirms the feature exists. The menu wording changes between versions, so look for the split option in the tab menu rather than trusting a fixed path.

Keyboard shortcuts speed up the back and forth. Use ⌘T for a new tab, ⌘W to close one, ⌘⇧T to reopen a tab you closed by mistake, and ⌘L to jump to the address bar. Use ⌘F to find a supplier name on a long statement page. Those five cover most of a close.

Here is a simple pattern. Put the supplier statement on the left and the ledger on the right. Search the statement for an invoice number with ⌘F. Then switch to the ledger and search for the same number. Two searches replace a long scroll through both lists.

blocks.title: Stale tabs
blocks.text: A ledger tab left on an old filter looks like current data. Before you copy a balance, refresh the page and check the date range. Close or rename the group when the client's work ends.
Print and save PDFs from Chrome on Mac without surprises

Press ⌘P to open the print window. Google's Chrome help page confirms ⌘P and says you can also go through File > Print. Choose a destination, then read the preview before you save or send anything. The preview is the cheapest check you have.

The PDF option lives in the destination menu of the print window. Look for Save as PDF there. Google's help page does not describe that option, and menu wording can shift between versions, so read the menu on your own screen. The same page does not describe margins, headers and footers either. Test those controls on a single page before a deadline.

Name the file before you save. Use the client, the period and the document type, such as Client name, March, bank statement. A clear name sorts well in a folder, and a reviewer can find it without opening it. For Google Sheets, the export steps are different, so see [our guide to exporting a sheet as PDF](/how-to/export-as-pdf-in-google-sheets).

blocks.title: Check the page first
blocks.text: Cookie banners, side menus and sticky headers can appear in a printed page. Use the preview to spot them. If the software offers its own report export, that output can be cleaner than a browser print.
Extensions for accountants in Chrome and what to check first

Extensions add features to Chrome. Dextension is one example for accountants. Dext says it puts Dext inside Xero and QuickBooks Online, so you can handle documents, transaction coding and reconciliation in one place. It works in Chrome or Microsoft Edge only, and you need an active Dext account.

Dext says the extension is free to use with a Dext subscription. The page does not say whether a paid plan is required, so check Dext's pricing before you rely on it. Chrome Web Store ratings were not checked for this guide, so read them yourself before you install.

headers: Check before you rely on it
rows: Confirm your suppliers use a portal it can reach
Compare that history with your current chart of accounts
Test one supplier before a full close
Check how the request reaches the client

blocks.text: A general rule applies to every extension. Install only what you use each week. An extension with access to a page can read what appears on that page. Remove the ones you installed for one job and forgot about.
What the research says about accountant time

The figures come from two sources, and they measure different things. The first is a Dext survey of 300 UK accountants, reported in March 2023. Dext sells software, and the article gives no fieldwork dates, so treat the numbers as directional. Nearly two fifths said over half their day goes to manual tasks.

The same survey found that 30% lack the tools to automate processes. It also found that 43% believe technology and software would make the job easier. In a separate question, 42% of accountants with 15 or more years in the industry named manual data entry and record keeping as the most painful part of the job when they joined. The article gives no current figure for that question.

The second source is a Stanford GSB and MIT Sloan working paper by Choi and Xie. Its summary article reports 8.5% less time on routine back-office processing for accountants who used generative AI. Those accountants also finalized monthly statements 7.5 days faster. The study used survey responses from 277 accountants and task-level data from 79 small and mid-sized firms.

The 8.5% covers routine back-office processing in general. It is not a data entry figure, so do not quote it as one. The article says the saved time can go to business communication, quality assurance and client-facing advisory work.
Ask Lazur out loud while you work in Chrome

Hold ⌥⌘, which is Option and Command together, and ask your question. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. It answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click for you. You do the clicking, and you keep control of the ledger. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Xero, Dext, QuickBooks or any other app. It has no partnership with those makers.

For notes, client emails and reminders, hold fn and dictate. Dictation writes clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. You can add snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots. Everyday tasks work by voice too, including timers, Apple Reminders and Calendar events.

Research works differently. Lazur runs background research in its own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Leave client names out of research questions unless you need them in that report.
On privacy, audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked and did stays on the Mac.
Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available. There is a free trial, and it needs no credit card. Plans and current terms are on the [pricing page](/pricing).
A worked example: matching a bank line in Xero

Say the bank feed sits in one tab and a supplier statement sits in the next. You see a payment that does not match a ledger line. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask, 'Where is the matching invoice on this statement?' Lazur circles the row and labels it. You read the label, then check the amount yourself.

Then ask, 'Walk me through matching this payment in Xero.' Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. You keep the coding decisions. If a line is unclear, ask Lazur to explain what it shows. It answers out loud, so your hands stay on the keyboard.
What Lazur will not do in your browser

items: Click buttons, fill in forms or submit anything for you.
Edit files or operate other apps on your behalf.
Work as a plugin or add-in inside Xero, QuickBooks or Dext.
Stand in for your review of figures, coding or client advice.

blocks.text: Common mistakes accountants make in Chrome on Mac
Most of these come from habit, not from Chrome itself. Check the list before a busy week starts.

items: One profile for every client, so logins and autofill cross over.
Printing without the preview, then sending a page with a banner on it.
Leaving another client's tabs open during a screen share.
Installing an extension from a search result without checking the publisher.
Skipping the About Chrome check, so the browser stays on an old build.
Trusting one version number from a single source. Check the build on your own Mac.

blocks.text: A first-week checklist for Chrome on your Mac

items: Open Chrome > About Google Chrome, and confirm the version and update status.
Create a work profile, and sign in there only.
Review saved passwords and Autofill entries, and delete old client data.
Make one tab group for each active client, and name every group.
Test ⌘P and the destination menu on one page before a deadline.
Check Dext's pricing and the Chrome Web Store before you install Dextension.
Try one Lazur question on a live page, starting with where something is.

blocks.text: When you are ready to try Lazur, the [download page](/download) is where to start.

faq.question: Is there a separate version of Chrome for accountants on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Accountants on Mac use the standard Google Chrome app. The useful setup comes from profiles, tab groups, print habits and the extensions you choose. Check your build under Chrome > About Google Chrome.

faq.question: Which Chrome version is current on Mac?
faq.answer: Sources disagree. WhatIsMyBrowser lists 156.0.8078.82, released 2026-11-04. Google's Chrome Enterprise and Education release notes list Chrome 152, dated September 1, 2026. Open Chrome > About Google Chrome to see your own build.

faq.question: How do I save a Chrome page as PDF on Mac?
faq.answer: Press ⌘P, then read the preview. Open the destination menu in the print window and look for Save as PDF. Menu wording can change between versions, so check your own screen. Google's help page confirms ⌘P and File > Print.

faq.question: Does Dextension work with Xero in Safari?
faq.answer: Dext says Dextension works with Xero and QuickBooks Online only in Chrome or Microsoft Edge. You also need an active Dext account to use it. Check Dext's product page before you install anything.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Xero for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It points at things, answers out loud and guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Is client data sent to AI providers?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: How do I clear Chrome data on a shared Mac?
faq.answer: Sign out of work profiles first. Then press ⌘⇧⌫ to open the clear browsing data window, or go through Chrome > Settings. Our guide walks through each option.
